text:
jess: Heads-up, Avenue9b (int4) canary showed a weird combo: p99 latency +70% and sporadic OOMs under batch 4. Also memory fragmentation creeping up over ~30m. Need triage.

kai: On it. Any quick reproduction steps? Surface logs?

jess: Repro: curl to /v1/generate with batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=512, prompt length ~600 tokens. Attached numbers: p50 45ms p95 210ms p99 420ms (vs baseline p99 ~250ms). OOMs after ~12-20 minutes.

linh: I ran a small canary. Turned prefetch off and reduced max_new_tokens to 256. Latency dropped ~20% and OOMs stopped in the 30m window. Worth investigating prefetch behaviour with this quant layout.

omar: Logs show repeated "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" followed by large free/alloc churn. Looks like KV cache not staying contiguous — fragmentation.

maria: Could be the int4 packing + kernel alignment causing small free blocks. Also we changed minibatch packing heuristics for int4 in the last runtime PR.

kai: Hypothesis: prefetch + larger batch = many concurrent KV allocations of slightly different sizes -> fragmentation. We can try: 1) soft-throttle batching, 2) fix alignment to 256B, or 3) use slot_reserve for this model.

jess: Before code changes can we validate quick config flips? I want a perf/quality delta table.

linh: Quick tests results (30m each):
- baseline (prefetch on, batch 4, max_new 512): p99 420ms, 2 OOMs
- prefetch off, batch 4, max_new 512: p99 330ms, 0 OOMs
- prefetch off, batch 2, max_new 512: p99 260ms, 0 OOMs
- prefetch off, batch 2, max_new 256: p99 220ms, 0 OOMs
Quality eval (held-out prompts): small ROUGE drop ~0.4 pts when max_new_tokens=256 vs 512, still within regression budget.

omar: Recommending conservative defaults for Avenue9b: batch_max=2, max_new_tokens=256, prefetch=false, slot_reserve=0.08. Also enable soft-throttle to avoid simultaneous large-kv allocs.

maria: +1. I'll open a runtime flag to override per-model packing alignment to 256B for int4 to reduce fragmentation (cheap CPU change).

kai: Proposed config diff to push to feature flags for canary (apply to model:avenue9b):
```
models:
  avenue9b-int4:
    batching:
      max_batch_size: 2
      soft_throttle: true
    generation:
      max_new_tokens: 256
    runtime:
      prefetch: false
      slot_reserve: 0.08
      int4_alignment: 256
```

jess: Nice. Can we run a 4-hour soak on canary with that config? I'll also add per-token latency histogram and mem-frag metric to the dashboard.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: started canary for models/avenue9b-int4 at sha=fa3b2e7 (config overrides applied)

linh: 1-hour in: p99 now 230ms stable, no OOMs, mem fragmentation metric flat. Token throughput reduced ~8% vs baseline batch=4 but p99 much better.

omar: We should capture process maps when fragmentation grows next time: run "pmap -x <pid>" and nvprof mem snapshots. I'll add a small script to the canary job.

maria: I'll PR the int4_alignment flip and add tests for allocation alignment. If that passes, we can try toggling back prefetch in a second-phase test to see if alignment alone helps.

jess: Owners/timeline:
- maria -> PR for int4 alignment (24h)
- kai -> monitor canary metrics + add dashboard panels (4h)
- omar -> attach pmap/nvprof to canary job (8h)
- linh -> run 4h soak and extended eval (6h)

jess: If soak stays clean, we'll roll config to prod in stagger (10% -> 30% -> 100%) over 48h. Document any quality delta in release notes.

kai: Quick note: add metric alert for mem_frag_ratio > 0.12 and p99 increase > 25% over baseline to auto-rollback.

linh: Agreed. Running extended eval now, will post final perf/QA table when done.

jess: Thanks team. Good work catching this early. :thumbsup:
